issues.body:
The one round-2 finding that carries forward. With the blocker fixed the leg can now plausibly run, but nothing in this PR shows that it has.

The sibling within10km.rq records "verified count-equal to sparq's expected.tsv (51) on the pinned 100k corpus" and documents (sq-a8anf) that an unverified Jena rendering silently returned all-zero counts and forced a retraction of the wave-1 timings. That same file states the premise this PR rests on — spatial:withinCircle "is NOT usable on this corpus: it needs geo:hasGeometry feature modelling ... (its spatial index indexes 0 items; follow-up bead sq-enfy3)". This PR supplies the modelling but never demonstrates the premise now holds.

Three things only a real run settles:
1. Index granularity. Jena's GeoSPARQL SpatialIndex is built from Feature->hasGeometry->Geometry->asWKT. The feature corpus contains BOTH that shape and a bare `<e/geometry> geo:asWKT` shape. If the indexer registers the feature only, COUNT is 51; if it also registers the geometry node, COUNT is 102 -> permanent count-disagree.
2. The units argument form. `uom:metre` is passed as a URI; Jena's spatial property functions are also documented taking the unit as a string literal. A rejected form is a query-build error, not a row.
3. The `-1` limit literal — whether withinCircle accepts it or rejects it at build time.

These degrade to ERROR or count-disagree rather than to a false number, which is why this is major and not a blocker. But the workload may still yield no usable row, and the header makes a factual claim ("returns the owning feature through its spatial index") that no observation in this PR supports.

Note too that the envelope's `timings` WITHHELD logic is not what the publisher reads: ingest-canonical-competitors.mjs builds `values` from the raw `<id>_tsv`, so a count-disagreeing indexed timing is still published as a number with a DIFF badge (same-box-table.tsx does not suppress the cell). The oracle marks rather than withholds.
issues.fix_hint: Run the leg once against the pinned jar and record the observation in the header in the sibling's form, e.g.: "verified count-equal to sparq's expected.tsv within10km (51) on the pinned 100k feature-modelled corpus, jena-fuseki-geosparql 5.4.0". If the observed count is 102, add a `?e geo:hasGeometry ?g .` guard to restrict to features and re-record. If `uom:metre` as a URI is rejected, switch to the string-literal form and record which one Jena accepted. Attach the run's JENA_INDEX_READY_S and the emitted envelope row to the PR so the claim is traceable.
issues.title: Still no recorded execution evidence: the query has never produced an observed count, unlike its sibling which pins "verified count-equal ... (51)"

issues.body:
start_fuseki's loop treats any non-success of the probe as "not ready yet" and keeps polling to FUSEKI_READY_S (default 300s). For the base leg with `ASK {}` that is correct — the only reason it fails is that the server is not up.

For the indexed leg the probe is `ASK { ?e spatial:withinCircle (51 0 10000 uom:metre -1) }`, which can fail for two structurally different reasons: (a) the spatial index is still building, which polling fixes, or (b) the query itself is invalid or permanently false — the wrong units form, a rejected -1 limit, an index that registered 0 items. Case (b) is indistinguishable from (a), so the run silently stalls the full 300s and then records `ERROR/server-not-ready`, attributing a query defect to the server. Given the major above, (b) is a live possibility on the very first real run, and the stall is paid by every geo-same-box invocation that reaches the jena leg.

This is the same wall-clock cost as the round-2 blocker, but now conditional on the query actually being wrong rather than unconditional — hence minor.
issues.fix_hint: Two-stage the probe: first wait for plain `ASK {}` on INDEX_PORT (server up), then poll the withinCircle ASK under a much shorter, separate cap (e.g. FUSEKI_INDEX_READY_S, default 60). If the server answers `ASK {}` but the feature probe never succeeds, the query is the fault — log that distinction and record `ERROR/index-probe-failed` rather than `server-not-ready`, and capture the adapter's stderr (currently discarded by `2>/dev/null`) into $TMP so the HTTP 400 body is diagnosable.
issues.title: The readiness probe cannot distinguish "index still building" from "query permanently invalid", so a mis-rendered property function costs the full 300s cap and is misreported as server-not-ready

issues.body:
The propagation is correct and byte-stable for existing envelopes (cc.sparq_oracle_workload / cc.corpus_variant are undefined there, so no committed snapshot moves) — I verified that. But grepping the whole tree, the only occurrences of either key outside the generated JSON are these two assignments. site/src/components/benchmarks/same-box-table.tsx renders query / rows / per-engine values / count_match and nothing else, so neither field reaches a reader.

The published table therefore shows a `within10km_indexed` row directly beneath `within10km`, both with `rows: 51`, one with a Jena number and an empty sparq cell, and no visible signal that (a) the 51 is borrowed from a different workload sparq actually ran, and (b) the timing came from a different corpus — 2x the triples, feature->geometry modelled — on a separate server. Only the suite-level `scale` string carries (b), two levels away from the row. Nothing false is asserted, but the single most load-bearing caveat for that row is not where the row is read.
issues.fix_hint: Surface both fields in same-box-table.tsx — the cheapest honest form is a marker on the query cell with the detail in a title attribute, e.g. render `{r.query}` plus a superscript dagger when `r.corpus_variant || r.sparq_oracle_workload`, with title={[r.corpus_variant, r.sparq_oracle_workload && `count oracle: ${r.sparq_oracle_workload}`].filter(Boolean).join(' — ')}, and add the corresponding optional fields to the SameBoxComparison row type in site/src/data/benchmarks.
issues.title: sparq_oracle_workload and corpus_variant are written into the generated data but no consumer renders them, so the caveat is invisible where it matters

issues.body:
FEATURE_CORPUS / FEATURE_TRIPLES default to "n/a" and are only overwritten inside the `JENA_STATUS = pending` branch — that part is the correct round-2 fix. But the envelope's `scale` is now formatted unconditionally as "...; Jena indexed-radius variant has %s triples and preserves the points with feature->geometry modelling (%s)".

On an ONLY=sparq run, or any run where the jar is absent and the leg gracefully skips, the emitted envelope reads "Jena indexed-radius variant has n/a triples and preserves the points with feature->geometry modelling (n/a)" — asserting a variant that was never built, in the field a reader uses to identify the substrate. It is not a false number, but it is a provenance string describing something that does not exist for that run.
issues.fix_hint:
Build the suffix conditionally in the Python block:
  scale = "fixed CRS84 point corpus, %s triples (%s)" % (npoints, corpus)
  if os.environ["FEATURE_CORPUS"] != "n/a":
      scale += "; Jena indexed-radius variant has %s triples ... (%s)" % (feature_triples, feature_corpus)
so an envelope only describes a corpus variant it actually generated.
issues.title: The scale string claims an indexed-radius variant even on runs that never build one ("has n/a triples ... (n/a)")

issues.body:
The `if [ ! -s "$FEATURE_OUT" ]` guard means points-feature-100000.nt is derived once and then reused forever. If OUT is ever regenerated with a different seed, window, or triple shape (the header warns these MUST stay in lockstep with bench_geo.rs), FEATURE_OUT is not rebuilt and silently keeps describing the old corpus. The gen.sh header notes CI may key actions/cache on /tmp/geo, so a stale derived file can outlive the run that produced it.

The new awk precondition guard closes the shape-drift-at-generation-time hole well (I confirmed NF==5 holds for the current generator and that Rust's f64 Display cannot introduce a second space), but it only runs when the derived file is absent.
issues.fix_hint: Invalidate on the source: regenerate when the derived file is older than its input, e.g. `if [ ! -s "$FEATURE_OUT" ] || [ "$OUT" -nt "$FEATURE_OUT" ]; then`. A stronger form is to key the filename on a short hash of OUT, but the -nt test is a one-line fix and matches how the direct corpus is already treated.
issues.title: The feature corpus is cached under /tmp/geo with no shape/version key, so a regenerated direct corpus will not invalidate a stale derived one

verdict.summary:
Round 3 resolves the round-2 blocker. I reproduced the fix: with `local default_ask='ASK {}'; local readiness_ask="${4:-$default_ask}"` the emitted query is byte-equal to the caller's argument both unset (`ASK {}`) and with a 4th arg — no stray brace. Every other round-2 item is addressed, each verified against the checkout rather than the diff prose:

- INDEX_FUSEKI_PORT is a documented, overridable env var.
- stop_fuseki escalates SIGTERM -> poll -> SIGKILL -> poll with FUSEKI_STOP_S configurable; wait_fuseki_stopped now tests real liveness (`kill -0` on the recorded PID, /dev/tcp only in port mode), so an adapter hiccup can no longer read as 'stopped'.
- FEATURE_CORPUS generation moved inside the `JENA_STATUS = pending` branch with n/a defaults, so ONLY=sparq no longer builds or caches the 2x corpus.
- gen.sh asserts the corpus precondition in awk (NF==5, `<...>` subject, asWKT predicate). Checked against generate_corpus (crates/sparq-geo/examples/bench_geo.rs:85-98): the WKT literal's single internal space yields exactly NF=5, and Rust's f64 Display never emits exponent notation, so the guard cannot false-abort a run.
- The readiness probe now exercises the spatial index itself, per the round-2 fix hint, so a data-loaded-but-not-indexed server can no longer report ready. The new `cut -f2 == 1` check matches the adapter's stdout contract (`engine\tcount\tquery_us`, ASK true -> count 1).
- sparq_oracle_workload and corpus_variant are propagated; rowCountMatch reads only cc.agree, so the added string keys cannot perturb it.

What blocks approval is unchanged in kind but smaller in scope: the new query has still never been executed, so the 51-vs-102 index-granularity question and the units/limit argument forms remain unverified — and within10km.rq documents (sq-a8anf) exactly this class of unverified Jena rendering forcing a retraction. Remaining: one major plus three minors and a nit, strictly fewer and lower than round 2.
